title: Lists and dictionaries
setup:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("games.csv")
explanation: Two Python containers show up everywhere in pandas. A list holds several items in order, inside square brackets: ["RPG", "Shooter"]. You get one item by its position, counting from 0: genres[0] is the first. len() tells you how many items there are. A dictionary (dict) stores pairs, each with a key and a value, inside curly brackets: {"Minecraft": 29.99}. You look up a value by its key: prices["Minecraft"]. You've already used a list: df[["title", "price"]] is a list of column names inside the picking brackets.

lines.explain: A list of 3 items, in order, inside square brackets.
genres[0] is the first item (Python counts from 0). len() counts the items. Output: RPG 3
A dictionary: each key (a game) is paired with a value (its price), inside curly brackets.
Look up the value for the key Minecraft: 29.99.

tasks.prompt: Predict first: what will this print?
hints: [0] is Minecraft, so [1] is the next one.

solution_lines.explain: Positions are 0, 1, 2. Position 1 is the second item: Fortnite.

tasks.prompt: Fill in the blank so the list cols holds the title and price column names, then show those columns.
hints: The second item is the name of the price column. It's text.

solution_lines.explain: A list of two column names.
Use the list to pick those columns: the same as df[["title", "price"]].

tasks.prompt: Make a dictionary called prices with Minecraft at 29.99 and Elden Ring at 59.99. Then print the price of Elden Ring.
hints: Curly brackets, with key: value pairs separated by commas. Then look up by key with square brackets.

solution_lines.explain: Look up the Elden Ring key: 59.99.

tasks.prompt: Dictionaries rename columns too. Rename release_year to year and show the first 3 rows.
hints: df.rename(columns={old name: new name}) takes a dictionary.

solution_lines.explain: The dictionary maps the old name to the new one. Then show 3 rows.

tasks.prompt: Build your own table! Use pd.DataFrame() with a dictionary: a column game with Minecraft and Fortnite, and a column hours with 120 and 45.
hints: Each key is a column name, and each value is a list of that column's values.

solution_lines.explain: A dictionary of lists becomes a table: keys are column names, lists are the column values.

recap: You just learned lists ([ ], counting from 0) and dictionaries ({key: value}), and saw how pandas uses them to pick columns, rename columns and even build tables.
